title: Check yourself: MCP clients, testing a server and debugging it

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A server's tools are not showing up in a host, and the team cannot tell why. Which first step does the documentation recommend?

options.text: Try it standalone in the Inspector, with no other application involved
options.says: The page says the guide's connection checks include "Test standalone with Inspector", and the guide calls the Inspector the "first stop" for debugging.

options.text: Write the server again in another language to rule out an SDK defect there
options.says: Ruled out because the steps go through logs, the process and "Test standalone with Inspector" before anything is rewritten.

options.text: Add output to stdout so that the host can see the server's progress
options.says: Ruled out because "Local MCP servers should not log messages to stdout (standard out), as this will interfere with protocol operation."

options.text: Reinstall the host application, since a corrupt cache hides tools
options.says: Ruled out because the documented checks look at the server and the logs, such as "Verify server process is running", and none of them is to reinstall the host.

questions.stem: A stdio server started by a host cannot find credentials that work in the developer's shell. Which documented behavior explains it?

options.text: Only a limited subset of variables is inherited
options.says: The page quotes the guide: "MCP servers launched over stdio inherit only a limited subset of environment variables automatically (the exact set is platform-dependent)."

options.text: Credentials reach a server only through its HTTP transport
options.says: Ruled out because the fix is to "set an env key in the host's configuration", whatever the transport.

options.text: Variables arrive after the first tool call has completed
options.says: Ruled out because a start-up failure can be "a missing environment variable", so the variables matter from launch and not after a first tool call.

options.text: The host clears the whole environment before each launch
options.says: Ruled out because servers "inherit only a limited subset of environment variables automatically", which is some of them, not none.

origin.section: Where a server fails in front of a host

questions.stem: A CI job must exercise a server without a browser and print machine-readable results. Which Inspector client fits?

options.text: The web one, the graphical default
options.says: Ruled out because the web one is "A full graphical inspector in the browser. The default, and the richest surface."

options.text: The terminal one, an interactive interface
options.says: Ruled out because the terminal one is "An interactive terminal UI, for when a browser isn't available or wanted."

options.text: The CLI one, built for scripted use
options.says: The page's table says the CLI is "A scriptable, machine-readable client for CI, shell pipelines, and coding agents."

Ruled out because only the CLI is "A scriptable, machine-readable client for CI, shell pipelines, and coding agents.", while the other two are graphical or interactive, even though every client behind the Inspector "connects the same way".
